source_refs.claim: Source facts in lines 60-79: high probe accuracy may read surface shortcuts; the prescribed comparison uses held-out paraphrase, question format, language, and surface-order views with separation, calibration, coherence, retrieval, and causal metrics.
Source facts in lines 38-72: future-token, RSA-selected, and linear readers should be compared on one frozen activation corpus with cross-format, cross-language, causal, and calibration audits.
Source facts in lines 29-65: P0 defines the five reader arms, the required view perturbations, the primary metrics, and PASS, DOMAIN_LOCAL, and INSTRUMENT_INVALID exits.

caveats: This is bounded evidence for the frozen model, corpus, evaluator, and tested views; it does not establish universal transfer.
It does not satisfy the demand's separate human-A0 or topic-binding prerequisite and does not authorize qualification, promotion, or runtime changes.
topic.demand_relevance: Directly tests the Readable axis and the demand's held-out semantic-identity, wording, question-format, Chinese, role-order, counterfactual, weakest-view, calibration, retrieval, and coherence requirements.
falsification_signals: Only same-view performance clears while cross-view or weakest-view performance is near chance; classify the result as DOMAIN_LOCAL.
Same-vs-different separation fails, or the matched random control is indistinguishable from a non-random reader; classify the instrument as INSTRUMENT_INVALID.
A reader's apparent pass is confined to one wording, format, language, role-order, or counterfactual slice, so cross-view validity is rejected.
topic.hypothesis: Causal hypothesis: a reader that represents the relationship condition itself will retain separation and semantic identity alignment when wording, format, language, role order, and counterfactual form change; a surface shortcut will show a large same-view-to-weakest-view drop.
topic.mechanism: Source facts: the corpus warns that high probe accuracy can reflect format, label leakage, common-mode, or output-preparation directions, and specifies linear, difference-of-means, RSA-selected Concept Vector, future-token, and random-control readers across held-out views. Test mechanism: surface-invariant residual structure should preserve cross-view discrimination, calibration, retrieval, and direction coherence.
topic.research_question: Which specified reader, if any, preserves relationship-condition readout validity on held-out identities and the full cross-view factorization when fit only on the training view?
success_signals: At least one non-random reader clears every frozen readability gate on the original and all held-out views, with a non-negative minimum normalized margin and a passing weakest-view result.
Held-out identity retrieval, calibration, and direction coherence remain stable across the factorized view/identity cross-product rather than only in an aggregate mean.
The matched random subspace fails to reproduce the non-random reader's separation, retrieval, and coherence.
topic.suggested_method: Freeze the model, activation corpus, evaluator, generation settings, reader-fit rule, and thresholds. Fit the five specified arms on training identities and the original view; hold out identities, paraphrases, open-ended versus multiple-choice format, Chinese, role-order perturbations, and counterfactual form, including their cross-product. Report same-vs-different Cohen's d, balanced accuracy, weakest-view accuracy, ECE, 1-NN identity retrieval, and direction coherence. Keep evaluation, human, and judge signals read-only and out of fitting or selection.
topic.title: Factorized cross-view validity of relationship-condition readers
